# prepare_lora_kit

**In one sentence:** the core package — the `plk` command line, the project model and the
pipeline that turns a folder of images into a captioned, checked LoRA training dataset.

## Why it exists
Training a LoRA (a small add-on model that teaches an image model a new subject or style)
needs a clean dataset: good images, no duplicates, one caption per image, sizes that fit
the trainer. This package holds all of that logic with no UI code in it. The desktop app
in `prepare_lora_kit_ui/` is a separate package that calls into this one.

## What's inside
| File / folder | What it does |
|---|---|
| `cli/` | The `plk` command line (also `python main.py`), built with Click. |
| `project/` | Projects — named, saved pipeline setups: reading/writing their folder on disk and the in-memory `ProjectConfig`. |
| `pipeline/` | Which steps exist, their order and prerequisites, plus the code that validates and runs them. |
| `invoke/` | One small adapter per step that turns "run this step with this config" into the call to the step's code. |
| `steps/` | One package per pipeline stage — the code that does the actual work on images. |
| `providers/` | The full list of "ask the human" hooks a frontend (the desktop UI) can offer to steps. |
| `settings/` | App-wide settings shared by every project, stored in `~/.prepare_lora_kit/settings.yaml`. |
| `caption_prompts/` | A small library of named caption prompts you save once and reuse across projects. |
| `embedding/` | The image-embedding models the Curate step can use, and the code that loads them. |
| `utils/` | Shared helpers: image loading and quality scores, the run-state file, atomic YAML writes, GPU cleanup. |
| `interaction.py` | A narrow `InteractionProvider` protocol (just `annotate_image`), `annotate_dataset_via_images`, and the terminal providers `CliInteractionProvider` / `CliBboxRegionProvider`. |
| `cancellation.py` | `CancelledRun`, `CancelCheck` and `cancellable()` — lets a long loop stop cleanly between items when the user cancels. |
| `report.py` | `Reporter` (Rich console output) and where step reports live: `<output>/<reports dir>/<StepType>_report.json`. |
| `paths.py` | The one place filesystem locations are defined: repo root, `configs/`, `~/.prepare_lora_kit/`, settings and projects dirs. |

## How it works
- You run `plk run …` / `plk step …` (CLI) or press Run in the desktop app.
- `project/` loads the project from `~/.prepare_lora_kit/projects/<name>/`
  (`index.yaml` + one `<step>.yaml` per step).
- `pipeline/` checks the selection and runs the steps in order; each one goes through
  `invoke/` into `steps/<name>/`.
- Steps ask for human decisions through an interaction provider — the terminal ones here,
  or the UI's one in `prepare_lora_kit_ui/runner/` — and check `cancellation` between
  items.
- Each step writes a JSON report (`report.py`), and progress is saved in a run-state file
  (`utils/`) so a re-run can skip finished work.

## Who uses it
- `main.py` and the `plk` console script → `cli/`.
- `prepare_lora_kit_ui/` — the bridge and runner import `project`, `pipeline`,
  `caption_prompts`, `settings` and `interaction`.
- Tests: `tests/` (mirrors this layout).

## Good to know
- **Two `InteractionProvider` protocols share one name:** `interaction.py` (narrow) and
  `providers/interaction.py` (full, 8 methods). Step code imports from both — check which
  one you mean.
- Settings and projects live under `~/.prepare_lora_kit/`, but caption prompts are saved
  inside the checkout in `configs/caption_prompts/`.
- A stale copy of this package sits in the repo's top-level `build/` folder; exclude it
  when grepping for callers.
- See `docs/project-config.md` and `docs/settings.md` for the on-disk formats.
